title: Swim.com Workout Failure Rate
dataSources: Swim.com workouts (`swimcom:workout`), MySwimPro sessions (`myswimpro:session`), pool lap logs (`pool:lap`), and swim meet results (`swim:meet`).
app: Swim.com workout exports, MySwimPro session logs, pool lap counters, swim meet results, and interval pace trackers forwarded to Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=swimcom:workout
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(workout_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by stroke_type
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often Swim.com workout records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each stroke.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize workout_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per stroke.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It maps which parts of your Swim.com workout data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
